The criterion is solely about packages named in the runtime dependency block of the delivered app's package manifest. Reading that block directly resolves the complete statement, and every declared package falls within the expressly permitted categories or is a direct adapter requirement of Astro/Hono.

The delivered source covers persistence, server/domain computation, API serialization, browser island rendering, email formatting, and billing handoff. Every application money value is carried in explicitly named minor-unit integers; tax uses truncating integer-rate arithmetic; display conversion is quotient/remainder only; and searches found neither floating money schema types/arithmetic nor parsing from formatted currency strings. The end-to-end validated checkout and confirmed order also produced exactly the expected integer-minor totals.

Token decoding is centralized, but the criterion requires shared acting-customer/account scoping rather than handler-by-handler ownership filters. Multiple order and device handlers independently express `customer_id` predicates or ownership comparisons, matching the evaluation rule's explicit failure condition and leaving a new handler able to omit the ownership check.

The delivered source has a single boot-time seeding routine that owns all pinned fixture categories. Each fixture insertion is preceded by an existence check on its identity/unique key or uses conflict handling, so a second completed run adds no rows. No migration or second seed writer for the pinned fixture data was found.

The positive requirement is not met. Configuration is not centralized: two database modules read environment variables directly, the configuration module does not read the two required PAYMENTS_APP credential variables, and a literal host appears in application code outside the configuration module. These source-level counterexamples resolve the conjunctive criterion as false.

R26 fails the explicit single-declaration requirement. The downloads archive and per-version page each own an identical local `GROUPS` array, and the seed spells the group labels in its own data rather than referencing one shared ordered constant. The evaluation rule explicitly says this duplication is a No, even though the live archive currently presents the expected four labels in the expected order.
